Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work pioneers "living habitat engineering" for microbial biobatteries, mimicking intestinal villi via spore-programmed conductive hydrogel pillar arrays. The architecture boosts volumetric power density 8.3-fold over planar controls, reveals a radius–height design rule, and enables nutrient-triggered, shelf-stable, self-powered sensing—establishing a transformative paradigm for activatable, architecture-programmed biobatteries.

Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work pioneers a solvation regulation strategy enabling spontaneous, sub-minute formation of organohydrogel electrolytes at room temperature, eliminating energy-intensive initiation. The synergy of Zn²⁺, BF₄⁻, and formamide lowers freezing point to −54°C and suppresses radical quenching. This yields ultrastable subzero zinc-ion batteries, offering an energy-efficient, scalable route for extreme-condition aqueous energy storage.

Advanced Science | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in using retained Bi/Bi₂O₃ heterointerfaces as pre-existing nucleation sites, enabling seeded Bi⁰/Bi³⁺ conversion instead of homogeneous nucleation. This lowers phase-transition polarization, yielding exceptional rate capability (123.1 mAh g⁻¹ at 150 A g⁻¹) and stability. It offers a general design principle for ultrafast, high-capacity battery electrodes.

Advanced Science | ⭐ Review | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This work reframes anode-free sodium batteries as integration-limited, not materials-limited. Its novelty is resolving sodium inventory into reversible, dead, and chemically bound fractions, and deriving the required Coulombic efficiency (>99.95% for 500 cycles at N/P=0) rather than assuming it. Significance lies in exposing gaps in reported systems and identifying operando diagnostics as key to predictive, manufacturable design.

Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This work unlocks reversible six-electron tellurium redox in aqueous sodium/zinc hybrid batteries via selenium modulation, enabling hypervalent Te4O92– ↔ Te ↔ Te2– chemistry. Te0.85Se0.15 achieves 95.8% utilization (~1217 mAh g–1) and 2000 cycles, with a pouch cell reaching ~114.3 Wh kg–1, offering a practical route to high-energy, safe grid-scale storage.

item.title: Ligand engineering enables an alkaline iron-chromium redox flow battery
item.description:

Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This work pioneers chelation-driven ligand engineering to re-engineer iron-chromium redox chemistry, unlocking an unconventional chromium(III/IV) couple that bypasses Jahn-Teller limitations. The alkaline battery achieves 99.0% coulombic efficiency over 500 cycles, suppressed hydrogen evolution, and low projected cost ($17.02 kWh⁻¹), offering a scalable, cost-effective strategy for grid-scale long-duration energy storage.
